title: One current truth, kept by code
body: What is current and what is retired lives in ONE registry (whatifs/truth.py). Retired concepts are data: pattern, the context in which naming them is still true, and the truth that replaced them. The same scan runs in Plan Guard (every push), the test suite, the rehearsal and contract check docs_current (every episode).

evidence.source: Gloaguen et al., Evaluating AGENTS.md, arXiv 2602.11988
evidence.finding: agents obey repository context files; such files do not generally raise success and raise cost by more than 20%, so a wrong or long file is a direct loss
reliability falls as input grows; distractors close in topic to the answer hurt most (an old doc about the same system is exactly that)

title: Reference docs are rendered from the code, never typed
body: docs/CURRENT/SYSTEM.md is generated by tools/gen_docs.py (facts, checks, key settings, jobs, tabs, modules). A test fails when the committed file differs, so a doc cannot state a number the code does not hold.

evidence.source: Grafana Loki CI step: check generated documentation
evidence.finding: CI fails when generated reference docs differ from the committed file
derive docs from one definition; treat drift as a build failure

title: History is archived whole and marked, never deleted and never followed
body: Old docs move to docs/ARCHIVE under the first line 'HISTORICAL - DO NOT FOLLOW. Superseded by ...'. The text under the header is unedited. Current docs may name the archive only while saying it is history.

evidence.source: M. Fowler, Architecture Decision Record (bliki); Backstage ADR docs
evidence.finding: accepted records are never rewritten or deleted; they are superseded with a pointer to the replacement

title: Ratchet baseline for unavoidable mentions
body: Code that must name an old value (a one-time setting move) is listed in truth.BASELINE by file and rule with a count and a reason. One more hit fails; one fewer also fails until the entry is pruned. The list can only shrink.

evidence.finding: baseline existing violations by count per file and rule; report new ones at once; prune stale suppressions

title: CLAUDE.md is short, rules only, and wording is not enforcement
body: CLAUDE.md holds only the non-obvious rules of this codebase and stays under 200 lines; everything else is in docs/CURRENT. Every rule that matters also has a check, because a context file is context, not enforcement.

evidence.finding: target under 200 lines; specific and concise instructions are followed more reliably; CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration
repository overviews do not help; only non-standard practices are worth writing

title: B1 build takeaway
body: WORKED: making the generated doc pass the retired-concept scan surfaced real stale statements inside live settings notes that no grep of docs would have found (the learning-core note still named the outlier library; the publish-days note still cited the old cap). Scanning what the code SAYS about itself beats scanning documents. WATCH: line-based rules with an 'unless' context are precise only while sentences stay on one line; keep current docs one fact per line. WATCH: inline code comments still carry version labels (declared history in CLAUDE.md); if a future chat is seen acting on one, extend the scan to comments.

evidence.finding: first scan: 33 retired-concept hits + 11 dead paths across CLAUDE.md, ledger, build prompt, Mission Control guide and 5 settings notes; after B1: 0

title: Launch cadence: 4 long videos a month, one a week
body: Owner, 10 Nov 2026, answer to the question 'Launch month: 4 long videos (your agreed plan) or up to 8 (what the code allows today)?': "4 a month". Each long video is built to break out; daily Shorts and the two spin-offs carry the volume. Changing this needs the owner.

evidence.source: owner message in the build session

title: Executing a decision = retiring what it replaces
body: When a decision replaces a value, register the old value in truth.RETIRED before searching by hand. The scan found a fourth viewer line with the old cadence that a manual search missed, and the generated system doc is what exposed the ledger-versus-code mismatch in the first place.

evidence.finding: manual search found 3 of 4 lines; the retired rule found the 4th on its first run
